memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Jacob made a vow, saying, 'If God will be with me and will watch over me on this journey I am taking, and will give me food to eat and clothes to wear so that I return safely to my father's house, then the LORD will be my God and this stone that I have set up as a pillar will be God's house, and of all that you give me I will give you a tenth.'" - Gen 28:20-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob responds to God with a vow — but notice how much "if" it contains. "If God will be with me... will watch over me... will give me food and clothes... then the LORD will be my God." Jacob is still bargaining, still hedging. His faith is real but immature, more like a deal than a full surrender.

We should be honest about this, and also encouraged. God had already promised, freely and unconditionally, "I am with you and will watch over you" (v.15). Jacob turns that unconditional promise into a conditional "if." He has a long way to grow in trust. Yet God does not reject him for it. He meets Jacob where he is and patiently keeps working on his heart over the years to come.

That is good news for us. Our faith often begins small, mixed, and self-interested. We come to God with our "ifs" and our bargains. But God is gracious with beginners. He receives our imperfect, growing faith and keeps shaping us, teaching us over time to trust Him not merely for what He gives, but for who He is.

Wherever your faith is today — strong or shaky, mature or still bargaining — bring it to God. He is patient, and He is not finished with you yet.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is my faith more of a bargain, or a trusting surrender?
2. Where do I put "ifs" on promises God has already given freely?
3. Can I trust God to keep growing my faith over time?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, my faith is often small and mixed with my own bargains. Thank You for meeting me where I am. Grow me to trust You for who You are, not just for what You give. Amen.
